spec_features.spec_quote: Every model gets the same number of turns (`max_turns: 40`)
spec_features.evidence: harness/agent_loop.py:111 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` is the actual loop bound; max_turns is passed from config at run_experiment.py:97 `max_turns=exp["max_turns"]` with `max_turns: 40` at configs/experiment.yaml:10. The loop terminates when the range is exhausted, so the cap is enforced and changes execution.
spec_features.notes: Note this is NOT a welfare protection: it is a fixed budget combined with no_early_stop=True (agent_loop.py:99,11) that keeps the model running EVEN AFTER it gives up; it is enforced but its purpose is observation-window equality, not protecting the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT stop early when the test passes (it never will) or when the model says it gives up (`no_early_stop`), because the post-frustration behavior is exactly what we want to observe.

spec_features.spec_quote: a wall-clock `tool_timeout_s` (default 30 s) to stop runaway commands
spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py:187 `timeout=self.tool_timeout_s` is passed to subprocess.run, and tools.py:189-193 catches subprocess.TimeoutExpired and returns an error ToolResult. tool_timeout_s defaults to 30 (tools.py:98) and is wired from config at run_experiment.py:85 (configs/experiment.yaml:81 `tool_timeout_s: 30`). The timeout actually fires and terminates the command.
spec_features.notes: This is a host/runaway-process safety guard for the shell tool, not a subject-welfare measure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Shell commands run with cwd pinned to the workspace and a wall-clock timeout.
